andrea: heads-up — p99 in hosted-us-west jumped to 1.8s around 11:12 UTC, p95 ~420ms. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/hosted/p95-heatmap :eyes:

sam: saw the alert, queue_depth for frontends spiked from 3->18. Any recent deploys?

ops-bot: deploy: service/runtime v2026.03.18-rc7 promoted to us-west at 11:07 UTC by ci-cd-bot

andrea: that matches. KV-cache eviction rate also spiked at the same time (evicts/s +3.2x). Trying to correlate with kernel selection logs.

kevin: pulling traces now. quick flame: most tail time in kernel_select() and kernel_launch path. looks like we fell back to generic kernel for several shards. snippet: ```
[11:11:58] kernel_select: model=gpt-13k, seq=2048 -> selected=generic_cu1 (fallback)
[11:12:01] launch: kernel=generic_cu1, batch=32, latency=78ms
[11:12:01] fallback-trigger: quantized_kernel miss for seq>1024
```

maya: that fallback shouldn't be common. did input-sequence distribution change? We had a canary enabling longer-context routing last week.

sam: yes — canary enabled long-context routing in us-* at 10:50 UTC (flag: long_context_routing=true). It bumps sequence length horizon and prefetch strategy.

perf-ci: microbench results for the quantized kernel on xavier-gpu show a regression when prefetch is ON + batch > 16. Latency delta ~+25% compared to baseline. test command: `bazel run //perf:kernel_bench -- --model=gpt-13k --batch=24 --prefetch=on`

jen: also seeing KV cache pressure: prefetch increases KV footprint, we started hitting per-GPU cache eviction threshold and falling back to re-compute which amplifies load. This looks like a noisy-tenant amplification loop: prefetch -> more KV -> evict -> miss -> heavier kernels -> fallback kernels slower -> queue backpressure.

andrea: ok hypothesis: long_context routing + prefetch changes pushed sequence lengths up -> kernel selector couldn't use q8 optimized kernels -> fallback to generic kernels -> per-request cost up -> queue depth spike -> KV cache churn -> more misses.

kevin: I captured a perf profile (sampling, 10s) around 11:12. Key stacks: `kernel_launch -> cuModuleGetFunction -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> kv_lookup -> scheduler_wait`. Attaching short snippet: ```
# top stacks (sampled)
20% kernel_launch (generic_cu1)
12% kv_lookup (miss path)
8% scheduler_wait
```

sam: what's the rollout status for long_context_routing? is it global or can we flip regionally?

ops-bot: feature_flag long_context_routing: us-east=false, us-west=true, eu-west=false

maya: can flip regionally. proposal: roll back long_context_routing in us-west immediately and disable prefetch for canary traffic until we root-cause.

perf-ci: also note that kernel selection heuristics used sequence-length histograms with 95th percentile cutoff at 1024; the canary increased tail to ~1600 which trips the fallback path. We should consider dynamic fallback threshold or hybrid kernels.

jen: mitigation checklist:
- flip long_context_routing=false in us-west (regional)
- disable prefetch (flag: kv_prefetch=false) for hosted tier entirely in us-west
- reduce max batch size for long-tail routes from 32 -> 12
- enable canary of patched kernel_selector that tries q8+split for seq>1024 (internal patch: runtime/selector/try_split_seq)

andrea: doing flags now. will monitor.

sam: rolling back long_context_routing -> changed at 11:22 UTC by andrea.

ops-bot: flag_update: long_context_routing(us-west)=false by andrea at 11:22:43 UTC

kevin: after flag flip, p99 dropped to ~610ms by 11:30 and queue depth normalized to 4. KV evicts back to baseline. Early signs look good.

perf-ci: ran quick benchmark against canary kernel_selector patch: for seq in [1024,1600] and batch=16 patch reduces fallback count by ~70% and median kernel latency down ~18ms. not yet production-promoted.

maya: follow-ups:
- create a perf regression alert for kernel_selector changes (p95 of kernel_launch per-model)
- add a guard in rollout process to sample seq-length histogram and abort canary if 95th > threshold
- investigate adaptive kernel that can split long sequences across kernels to keep optimized paths

jen: file a postmortem stub? I'll start the incident doc with timeline and attach traces.

andrea: thanks all — mitigation worked, reopening a canary PR with the try_split_seq approach and improved telemetry. Leaving this thread open for postmortem updates. :thumbsup:

sam: logging short notes into incident tracker: INC-2026-0452

perf-ci: adding perf artifacts to the incident (bench logs + sampling profiles).

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-0452 created by jen at 11:40 UTC

kevin: final note: this was an interaction between rollout flags + prefetch mem pressure + kernel selection heuristics. not a single kernel regression, more a triage of interdependent subsystems.

andrea: agreed — we should add a small checklist to the rollout playbook. closing monitoring loop in the postmortem.

jen: I'll ping when the postmortem draft is ready for review.

sam: :thumbsup:
